why: A reading is not just a number. Where it came from decides what may be done with it, and a record that cannot tell a measured value from a typed one from a reported one is a record that will eventually be read wrongly by somebody in a hurry.

provenance.name: Measured by a device
provenance.detail: Read off a paired instrument and written straight into the record. The instrument, its serial and the date it was last calibrated travel with the reading.
provenance.trust: The strongest of the four, and only while the calibration is in date. An instrument out of calibration still produces a reading; what it stops producing is a reading anybody should act on without saying so.

provenance.name: Entered by a clinician
provenance.detail: Read off an instrument by a person and typed in, or taken by hand. Attributed to the registration of whoever typed it.
provenance.trust: As good as the person and the instrument they were holding. It is not weaker than a device reading — a manual blood pressure is a clinical skill — but it is a different fact and the record says which.

provenance.name: Reported by the patient
provenance.detail: What the person said, in the record as what they said rather than as a finding.
provenance.trust: Not a measurement. It is evidence about the person's experience, which is often the more useful thing, and it must never be presented as though a clinician observed it.

provenance.name: Calculated
provenance.detail: Computed from other readings — BMI from height and weight, a mean arterial pressure from a blood pressure.
provenance.trust: Exactly as good as its inputs, and it names them. A derived value whose inputs are unknown is not a value.

devices.name: Blood-pressure monitor
devices.note: Cuff size is a clinical decision the device cannot make. A reading taken on the wrong cuff is wrong in a direction nobody can correct for afterwards, so the cuff used is recorded with the reading.

devices.name: Pulse oximeter
devices.note: Reads high on dark skin under low perfusion. This is documented rather than corrected for, because the correction is not the platform's to invent.

devices.name: Infrared thermometer
devices.note: Site matters and is recorded: a forehead reading is not an oral one.

devices.name: Glucose meter
devices.note: Strips expire separately from the meter, and an expired strip reads low. The strip lot travels with the reading.

devices.name: Weighing scale
devices.note: Recorded with whether the patient was weighed standing, seated or in bed, because the three are not comparable.

devices.name: Single-lead ECG
devices.note: A single-lead trace is a screening tool. It is never a diagnosis, and any interpretation is decision support that a doctor signs or does not.

captureStates.name: Captured
captureStates.detail: Taken, and held on the device it was taken on. It exists nowhere else yet.

captureStates.name: Waiting to send
captureStates.detail: Finished and sealed, waiting for a connection. The nurse has done everything they can do.

captureStates.name: Sending
captureStates.detail: In flight. Interruptible without loss — an entry that does not land stays queued.

captureStates.name: Stored
captureStates.detail: Accepted by the server and in the record.

captureStates.name: Needs a decision
captureStates.detail: Landed against a record that already holds a reading for the same observation in the same visit. Nothing is merged and nothing is discarded.

captureStates.name: Refused
captureStates.detail: The server would not take it, and says why. It stays on the device until somebody decides what to do with it.

conflicts.name: Two readings, one observation
conflicts.detail: The same observation recorded twice in one visit — usually a retake after a doubtful first reading. Both are kept; a clinician says which stands, and the other stays visible as superseded rather than being deleted.

conflicts.name: The device clock disagrees
conflicts.detail: A device that has been offline may have drifted or been set by hand. The server's receipt time is authoritative for ordering; the device's time is kept beside it as what the device believed, never presented as the time it happened.

conflicts.name: The record moved on
conflicts.detail: The record changed while the entry was queued — a doctor has already signed, or the visit was cancelled. It is never applied silently after the fact.

conflicts.name: The capturer's standing lapsed
conflicts.detail: A nurse whose clearance lapsed between capture and sync. The reading was taken while she was cleared, so it is not discarded — but it is not filed on her authority alone either.

rules.provenanceIsRequired: Every reading carries exactly one provenance. There is no default and no unknown: a value nobody can say the origin of is not filed.
rules.calibrationNeverRefuses: An out-of-date calibration marks a reading, it does not block it. A nurse in a home with one instrument still needs the number; what she must not have is the number without the caveat.
rules.deviceClockIsNotTruth: The device's own time is recorded as what the device believed. Ordering uses the server's receipt time.
rules.conflictsAreNotMerged: Nothing is auto-merged and nothing is auto-discarded. A timestamp does not win a clinical disagreement; a clinician does.
rules.queuedIsNotLost: An entry that has been captured is the nurse's work. It survives a crash, a restart and a sign-out, and it is never dropped to make a sync succeed.
rules.offlineNeverServesStaleSilently: A value read from the device's own store carries when it was written, on screen, in words.
